title: May the Grace of Christ Our Savior
description: May the Grace of Christ Our Savior in Tonic Solfa to RUSTINGTON, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 1 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 101, “2Cor 13:14”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RUSTINGTON; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: May the grace of Christ our Sa-vior And the Fa-ther's bound-less love, With the ho-ly Spi-rit's fa-vor, Rest up-on us from a-bove! Thus may we a-bide in u-nion With each oth-er, and the Lord; And pos-sess, in sweet com-mu-nion, Joys which earth can-not af-ford.

lines: May the grace of Christ our Savior
Thus may we abide in union
With each other, and the Lord;

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to RUSTINGTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
